Maya: heads-up — after merging Aquifer LoRA into the int4 variant the embedded responses skew for numeric/identity tokens. Quickpack results attached.

Rupert: can you paste the top-level diffs? Slices mattered previously.

Maya: short logs:
```
EVAL: embed_cos_sim(mean): base=0.893 -> merged_int4=0.721
EVAL: top1-acc (QA-format)=0.81 -> 0.58
WARN: token id 30112 collapsed to 301 -> OOV-like behavior
```
Also seeing low similarity on invoice-number examples.

Linh: oof that's a big drift. Did you run with KV-caching disabled? int4 codegen may be reordering per-layer scales.

Maya: ran with default serving config, kv_cache=true. Repro steps:
```
ri model checkout aquifer:loRA-merge
ri serve --model aquifer:int4-lora --batch 4 --kv-cache
ri eval quickpack --suite customer-invoice --out /tmp/aquifer-int4.json
```

Alex: try toggling `--quantize-scales per_channel` or run with `--force-fp16-kv`. Also add the embed baseline hash check:
```
python -c "print(hash_embedding(open('base_emb.pkl')))"
```

deploy-bot: deploy/aquifer-int4-lora started by Maya (req id d34f2). Status: in-progress :gear:

Rupert: good call on per_channel. If that doesn't fix, re-run merge with clamp folding (we had a similar fix on Delta customer a while back).

Sam: I can run a small sweep on CI. Assign me the task and the quickpack config.

Maya: assigning to @Sam — quickpack is here: s3://ri-evals/aquifer/quickpack-v3.json. I'll try per_channel first and post results.

Linh: add a follow-up: if per_channel doesn't help, run the model through our `embed-regression` harness and pin the older LoRA weights for shadow compare. Keep me in loop.

Maya: will do. thanks :thumbsup:
